n: A cry many people feel: why, Lord, do you seem so far away? Why hide when we are in trouble? Scripture allows honest questions in prayer.
In arrogance the wicked hunt down the poor. The psalmist asks that they be caught in their own schemes.
The wicked boast about their cravings; the greedy curse and despise the Lord.

f.g: Better “the greedy man curses and spurns the Lord.”

n: In pride the wicked don’t seek God; there is no room for God in any of their thoughts.

f.w: God is not in all his thoughts
f.g: His whole outlook is “There is no God.”

n: He prospers at all times; God’s judgments are far beyond his notice, and he scoffs at his enemies.
He tells himself, “Nothing will shake me; I’ll never have trouble.” This is the self-confidence of the proud.
His mouth is full of curses, lies, and threats; trouble and evil sit under his tongue. Paul quotes this verse.

f.w: His mouth is full of cursing

n: He hides in ambush near villages, murdering the innocent from hiding, his eyes secretly watching for the helpless.
Like a lion in a thicket he waits to seize the poor, then drags them off in his net.

f.w: as a lion in his den

n: The helpless are crushed and collapse, falling under his strength.

f.g: The Hebrew is unclear; it may describe the victim being crushed, or the predator crouching to pounce.

n: He tells himself, “God has forgotten; he has hidden his face and will never see.”
The psalmist cries, “Arise, Lord! Lift your hand! Don’t forget the afflicted.”

f.g: A gesture of power and action.

n: Why does the wicked person despise God, thinking, “He won’t hold me accountable”?

f.g: You won’t call me to account.

n: But God does see the trouble and grief and takes it into his own hands. The helpless entrust themselves to him, for he helps the fatherless.

f.w: thou art the helper of the fatherless

n: Break the power of the wicked; call evil to account until none is left.

f.w: Break thou the arm of the wicked

n: The Lord is King forever; the nations will perish from his land.

f.w: The LORD is King for ever and ever

n: The Lord hears the longing of the humble, strengthens their hearts, and listens closely.

f.g: You will strengthen and encourage them.

n: He will defend the orphan and the oppressed, so that mere mortals of the earth will terrify no more.

f.g: Mortal man made of dust — weak compared with God.
